references.text: Jesus' direct call to the disciples to imitate his act of washing feet, linked to his role as Lord and Teacher.
The principle that a servant is not greater than his master, which Jesus draws from the very act of foot-washing.
Jesus' new command to love one another as he has loved them, which is the theological conclusion of the foot-washing as an example of self-sacrifice.
Jesus' self-description as the one who came to serve and give his life, which is the underlying motivation for the action in John 13.
The parallel in Mark's Gospel to Matthew 20:28, emphasizing that Jesus came to serve, a theme central to the foot-washing scene.
The context of the foot-washing where Jesus, knowing that he came from God and was returning to God, shows his love for those who were his own.
